name: i18n-catalog-integrity
question: Is the i18n catalog tree structurally sound -- every i18n/locales/<code>/<ns>.json parses, starts with _meta, has keys that are a subset of en's, matches en's {{placeholders}} per key, carries the CLDR plural categories its locale needs, contains no mojibake or leaked HTML entities -- and do the three generated locale tables still equal i18n/locales.json? (FR-FBR-34/39, Contracts C34/C35/C41)

assertion.asserts: Every runtime (widget, SPA, Rust) will read a consistent catalog: no key can render as a raw key, a broken placeholder, or a wrong-locale string because of a malformed or drifted catalog file, and all three runtimes agree on which 31 locales exist.
assertion.measures: Working-tree files only: (A) `scripts/i18n/gen-locales.py --check` exit code (the three locales.gen.* files byte-equal a fresh render of i18n/locales.json); (B) json.load succeeds on every i18n/locales/*/*.json and the first key is `_meta` with `language` + `status`; (C) for each non-en file, flattened dotted keys are a subset of the en file's, and the set of `{{name}}` tokens per key equals en's; (D) for locales with extra CLDR categories (ru, uk, pl, cs, sk: few/many; lv: zero), every key that has `_one` in en has those suffixes when the key is translated; (E) values contain no `Ã`/`â€` mojibake sequences and no `&`/`&#` entities.
known_gaps: Does not judge translation QUALITY or whether a value is still English (untranslated-authored) -- that is scripts/i18n/validate.py's soft class and translation-gap-status's MISSING count, deliberately advisory.
Checks the working tree, not HEAD: a catalog edited but not staged passes here and fails in CI only if committed -- accepted; the oracle runs at commit time via the finalize gate.

Placeholder equality is set-equality of {{name}} tokens; it cannot see a placeholder that was translated into prose (`{{count}}` -> `Anzahl`) if the translator ALSO dropped the braces -- caught only as a missing token, which it is.
Probe D checks presence of plural categories, not their grammatical correctness.

output.schema: PASS or FAIL <n> with probe-level offender detail (file + key). Exit 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL, 2 on environment failure. Vacuous-PASS when i18n/locales/ is absent.

consultation.typical_sessions_using: every commit that touches a catalog, the locale table, or a generated locale file; every PODS converge of the localization arc

consumer_scope: feedbackmonk: every worker on FR-FBR-34..40 and every later session adding a string. Green is the Stage-0/1/2 exit gate of the localization plan.
fallback: python scripts/i18n/gen-locales.py --check; then for f in i18n/locales/*/*.json: python -c 'import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))' f; then diff the flattened key sets against i18n/locales/en/<ns>.json by hand.

provenance.authored_by: UI-localization LD (Stage 0 Task Zero, 2026-09-06). Assertion block frozen BEFORE any probe existed; probes B-E implemented by worker W-T in Stage 1 against this block.
provenance.hardening_note: Stage 0 ships Probe A + B only (generated-table drift + parse/_meta). W-T MUST adversarially self-test: a placeholder mismatch in de/widget.json and a hand edit to locales.gen.ts must both go red before the oracle's version is bumped to 1.0.0.
provenance.rationale: Three runtimes read one catalog tree written by two different actors (developers in en/, a machine-translation script everywhere else). A malformed file or a drifted generated table is invisible at build time -- the SPA and widget fall back to English silently and Rust compiles the bytes in -- so the only moment to catch it is the commit. DEC-FBR-17's 'partial catalogs are always shippable' promise rests on this check.
